reviews.text: Thank you for your consistently kind and attentive support.

Thank you for everything.

I believe this is the most trustworthy hospital.

All the doctors are excellent.

We received care from them since our child was a baby, and last week we were able to say goodbye peacefully at home.

We were able to spend 14 years together with peace of mind. Thank you.

I've been a patient here for over 10 years now. This hospital is excellent. I highly recommend it. When my previous dog was in a traffic accident, the head veterinarian, even though it was outside of regular hours and he had many other patients, went to great lengths to find a specialist for us. He was incredibly kind and caring. After that dog passed away, we got a new one, and we've been taking him to Clover Hospital from the start. Dr. Watanabe and all the nurses are very trustworthy, so if you're unsure where to go, I highly recommend you give them a try.

My cat was being treated at the vet.

Even though her kidneys were failing, they wouldn't administer subcutaneous fluid therapy, which made me suspicious, so I took her to another hospital. The first thing they said was, "With these kidney values, she needs subcutaneous fluid therapy immediately." After transferring her to that hospital, she recovered for a while.

All living things eventually pass away. But I want to be able to say goodbye to my cat knowing that I've done everything I could to treat her and have no regrets.

This experience taught me how incredibly important choosing the right hospital is.

While there are many excellent doctors and staff, including the head veterinarian, it can be disappointing when you end up with a disappointing primary veterinarian.
My pet didn't get any better, and there were also medication errors, which led to my growing distrust and a visit to a different animal medical center.
There, they changed the treatment plan, and my pet is now completely healthy.
I am very grateful for the head veterinarian's skills, but there are also doctors who take advantage of that and are unable to think for themselves, so I feel it's difficult to feel completely at ease going there, especially considering post-operative care.
The director of Clover Animal Hospital has a godly skill. I am grateful that he listens carefully during examinations.

Thank you for your care over the past 16 years. You never pressured me into unnecessary surgery and always listened to my feelings. In the end, she passed away in my arms, purely by chance. It was a very happy and joyful 16 years. When I called to cancel my next appointment, you asked, "Would you like us to make Momo-chan look beautiful?" It was my first time, and I didn't know anything about it, but I agreed. When Momo-chan came back, she was so cute, almost as if she were still alive, and tears welled up in my eyes. Then, a few days later, I received beautiful flowers, and my heart was filled with gratitude. Thank you so much. I hesitated to call you when you are so busy, so I wanted to express my gratitude in this message. Thank you, Dr. Watanabe, Dr. Kato, and all the staff.

About a 15-minute walk from Futako-Tamagawa station?

It's located in a high-end residential area.

They are understanding of rescued cats and I appreciate that they provide treatment with minimal use of sedation.

I came to the clinic after reading reviews.
My dog ​​was bleeding after a walk, so I went in, but initially, there was no concern whatsoever.
The first thing the middle-aged woman at the reception desk said was, "We can see him, but we'll finish with the scheduled appointments during your waiting time, so there will be an after-hours fee of 5000 yen + tax? Would you like to register?"
She didn't even ask, "Are you sure?" I thought, "Ah, so this is the kind of hospital it is..." and left without requesting treatment.

It's a shame, considering the positive reviews on Google.

It was unpleasant to see the receptionist, who is the face of the hospital, behave like that. Especially since they deal with animals.

They should have a more friendly receptionist.

You really can't know until you actually go!
